tasks.gr8-forces-motion-and-measurement-t4: Topic: Forces, motion and measurement. Cover speed, distance, time, simple motion calculations, friction, gravitational force, magnetic force, and electrostatic force. Ask Grade 8 learners to calculate speed, identify force types in scenarios, and reason about how forces affect movement.
tasks.gr8-forms-and-transfer-of-energy-t4: Topic: Forms and transfer of energy. Cover heat, light, sound, chemical, electrical, and mechanical energy, plus conduction, convection, radiation, and conservation of energy. Ask Grade 8 learners to trace energy transfers, compare heat-transfer pathways, and explain everyday energy systems.
tasks.gr8-beyond-the-solar-system-t4: Topic: Beyond the Solar System. Cover a galaxy as a collection of stars held together by gravity, the Milky Way as a spiral with the Sun near its edge in one arm (billions of stars; a hazy path of light across the sky), the Sun as the nearest star and Alpha Centauri (4,2 light years, the brighter Pointer of the Southern Cross) as the nearest easily visible star to the Sun, light minutes, light hours and light years (a light year is the distance light travels in one year, about 10 trillion km, so Alpha Centauri is 42 trillion km; the Earth is about 8 light minutes from the Sun; the Solar System is about 13 light hours across), and billions of galaxies in the observable Universe (estimated about 28 billion light years). Use the CAPS values and quote them in each question that needs them. Ask Grade 8 learners to explain and to convert with these values.
tasks.gr8-looking-into-space-t4: Topic: Looking into space. Cover seeing planets and stars by eye, constellations (the Southern Cross, Orion), stories and names from different cultures, telescopes forming an image and magnifying it, optical telescopes focusing light by refraction (lenses) or reflection (mirrors) such as SALT and the Hubble Space Telescope, radio telescopes focusing radio waves by reflection with a metal dish such as the SKA, and the good conditions for looking into space (cloudless skies, limited light and air pollution) found in many places in South Africa. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify the telescope types and the conditions.
